source_caption: Delve into the imaginative vision of Alexander McQueen’s Spring/Summer 2005 collection, “It’s Only a Game.” The runway metamorphosed into a symbolic battlefield where cultural worlds collided, merging Edwardian silhouettes with the intricate artistry of Japanese kimonos and the laid-back influence of American sportswear. Inspired by Peter Weir’s “Picnic at Hanging Rock,” the presentation featured thirty-six innovative ensembles, narrating a story of contrasting realms. The finale spotlighted models as colossal chess pieces in a masterfully choreographed dance staged by Les Child, epitomizing the cultural confrontation between East and West. At its peak, the game revealed two queens, embodied by models Gemma Ward and Hana Soukupouva, culminating in a powerful checkmate moment. The collection’s poignant theme of cultural clash was stunningly visualized, leaving an indelible impression of elegance and confrontation.
